# UNIX compress fixtures

These fixtures contain project-owned JSON and TAR payloads created for issue #3628. The payloads,
fixture generator, and encoded files use the repository's Apache-2.0 license. No third-party test
corpus data or encoder source is included. `provenance.json` records the exact encoded and decoded
SHA-256 hashes, sizes, mode, width, encoder arguments, and reference decoder for each fixture.

`document.json` is a short JSON object. `archive.tar` is a POSIX USTAR archive with that object as
`document.json`, followed by end-marker padding. `transitions.json` is a deterministic, seeded
base64-noise JSON object large enough to exercise dictionary growth through all widths from 9 to
16. Both encoded transition fixtures round-trip to the committed payload.

The block fixtures were generated with [ncompress 4.2.4.6](https://github.com/vapier/ncompress/tree/v4.2.4.6),
using `compress -c -f -b 16` with the payload on standard input. The source archive SHA-256 is
`112acfc76382e7b631d6cfc8e6ff9c8fd5b3677e5d49d3d9f1657bc15ad13d13`.

The non-block fixtures were generated by the project-owned `literal_lzw` function in
[`tests/compress_fixture.py`](../../compress_fixture.py) with `maxbits=16`. It emits literal codes
with the format's width-change alignment. This avoids a verified ncompress 4.2.4.6 `-C` encoder
bug: that option emits dictionary references using block-mode numbering under a non-block header.
Those broken outputs are not used as valid fixtures.

Every encoded fixture was decoded using GNU gzip 1.15 with `gzip -d -c`, and its output was
compared byte for byte to the committed payload. The
[GNU gzip 1.15 source archive](https://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/gzip/gzip-1.15.tar.xz) SHA-256 is
`9aa0cc780dec156b8282844833b342ab7cb08c25d2cd9a1869cdd0df31deff48`.
GNU gzip is not distributed with these fixtures.
